high-na-mask-roadmap.alt: Timeline from the 2026 announcement to the 2028 High-NA DRAM production target.
high-na-mask-roadmap.caption: Products and layers, yield, cost, and shipments are the next evidence to look for as the production plan moves forward.

high-na-mask-scale.alt: Comparison of the existing 6-inch photomask with the proposed 12-inch format.
high-na-mask-scale.caption: The planned size change applies to the photomask that carries the circuit pattern. Mask area alone cannot predict wafer throughput or cost.

high-na-process-chain.alt: Process sequence from mask and exposure through resist, development, etching, and electrical testing.
high-na-process-chain.caption: The micrograph documents an intermediate pattern. Post-etch defects, electrical characteristics, and yield are needed to establish manufacturing performance.

high-na-resolution-map.alt: The Rayleigh resolution equation and the links to resist behavior, etch transfer, and yield.
high-na-resolution-map.caption: A higher numerical aperture improves optical resolution. Resist response, stochastic defects, etch transfer, and final yield still require their own measurements.

nanoplasma-energy-boundary.alt: Comparison of device write energy calculated from voltage and current over time with the wider system energy budget.
nanoplasma-energy-boundary.caption: Device write energy covers what reaches the magnetic structure. The system total also includes the pulse generator, wiring, and read circuits.

nanoplasma-pulse-chain.alt: Signal flow from an on-chip nanoplasma pulse generator through the magnetic stack to state verification.
nanoplasma-pulse-chain.caption: The 6.4 ps interval is the electrical pulse width. A memory operation also requires address selection, signal propagation, and readout.

vdw-five-layer-selector.alt: Five-layer selector stack with graphene electrodes, molybdenum disulfide, and a central barrier.
vdw-five-layer-selector.caption: The five layers control access to a storage cell by suppressing current on unselected paths and passing current on the selected path.

vdw-metric-tradeoffs.alt: Nonlinearity, operating voltage, speed, endurance, and uniformity all affect array performance.
vdw-metric-tradeoffs.caption: A selector has to satisfy multiple requirements at once and retain its advantages across a large array.
